I am 47 years old, I went to primary school, and I have been working my own land for 30 years. My family has 10.1 mu on the North China Plain, and every year I do wheat in winter and maize in summer. I do not read research papers or go on the internet for farming advice. I talk to my neighbors, the input dealer in town, and I watch what works.

**My wheat this year:**

Last year I planted wheat on the full 10.1 mu. I used a good seed variety called Jimai 22 that I bought from the dealer — it is an improved seed, not the old kind my father used. It did well. The yield was around 550 kg per mu. This year I will do the same.

For fertilizer, last year I put down one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu at planting, and then I top-dressed twice with urea. That is about 7.5 kg of N from the compound, plus maybe 25 kg of urea per mu total, which is another 11.5 kg N. So that is roughly 19 kg nitrogen per mu. Some people in the village say that is a lot, but my neighbor Old Wang did the same and got 580 kg. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — if I lose yield, my whole year is ruined. So I will stick with 19 kg nitrogen per mu. The compound gives me about 7.5 kg phosphorus and 7.5 kg potassium per mu too. I know the soil here is a bit low on phosphorus because the dealer told me years ago, so I do not want to cut that.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing when it starts growing fast in spring, and once at grain filling. My well is good, the electricity is not too expensive, and I can handle three irrigations. I do rotary tillage before planting to break up the stubble from the maize.

Pesticide I spray twice — once for weeds right after planting, and once in spring for aphids or rust if I see them. If everyone else is spraying, I spray too.

**My maize this year:**

After I cut the wheat in early June, I plant maize immediately. I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958. Everyone around here uses it. It costs more than the old seed, but the yield is much better. Last year I got about 600 kg per mu. This year I hope for the same, maybe 610 kg if the weather holds.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at planting — again one 50kg bag of 15-15-15 per mu, so that is 7.5 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K. Then at the big trumpet stage I top-dress with urea, about 20 kg per mu, which is another 9 kg of nitrogen. So total nitrogen is about 16.5 kg per mu. I do not put more potassium because the compound gave some and my maize looked fine last year. Some people say put more, but fertilizer is real money — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — and I have eight mouths to feed and some kids in school. 16.5 kg N per mu is enough. I have done this for years and it works.

I irrigate maize two times: once right after planting if it is dry, and once at the trumpet stage or just before tasseling. Sometimes I do a third if it is very hot in August, but usually two is enough. The well can handle it.

For maize I till with the rotary tiller right after wheat harvest to bury the straw, then plant. Pesticide is two times: herbicide at planting, and one spray for corn borer in July. The corn borer can ruin everything if you ignore it.

**My whole budget thinking:**

I have 10.1 mu, which is not small but not big either. I do not hire much labor — my wife, my old father, and I do most of it. My two sons work in Shijiazhuang and send some money home, so I am not desperate, but every yuan counts. I will spend money on seed, fertilizer, and water. I cut costs where I can — I do not buy the most expensive pesticide, just the one that works and that the dealer has in stock. I watch what the neighbors do. If Old Wang and the family to the east both put 20 kg of N on their wheat, I will do about the same. I do not want to be the one who tries something different and fails.
